text:
infra-bot: 🔔 Pager: High NotReady count in cluster infer-pool-usw (>=3 nodes). Alert: kubelet restarts detected, pod restarts on inference namespace. Paging oncall. thread_ts=3723456789

maria: I'm on it, acked. Starting blast radius check.

kevin: confirming — seeing 4 nodes rotate to NotReady over last 10m.

sam: putting quick `kubectl get nodes` output:```
NAME                          STATUS     ROLES    AGE     VERSION
gke-infer-usw-1-abcde         NotReady   <none>   22d     v1.26.3
gke-infer-usw-2-abcde         Ready      <none>   22d     v1.26.3
gke-infer-usw-3-abcde         NotReady   <none>   22d     v1.26.3
gke-infer-usw-4-abcde         NotReady   <none>   22d     v1.26.3
```

maria: thanks — any obvious node-level OOMs or kernel messages?

kevin: grabbing kubelet logs from one NotReady node. tail:```
Mar 15 13:01:02 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU lockup - switching to software recovery
Mar 15 13:01:02 kubelet: E03015 13:01:05 eviction_manager.go:119] Pod evicted: memory available low, pod killer
Mar 15 13:01:06 kubelet: I03015 13:01:06 Node not ready: Kubelet stopped posting status
```

carla: seeing repeated `NVRM` and `GPU lockup` messages in dmesg on node. and some pods show `OOMKilled` + `cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction` in inference containers.

dylan: quick `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running` shows a bunch of `CrashLoopBackOff` and `OOMKilled`.

maria: initial hypothesis: GPU driver or host GPU resets causing kubelet churn and pod restarts. Could be kernel driver bug or thermal/power issue.

sam: mitigation play: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 3) fail traffic to other regions/pools 4) scale up spare capacity in eu-west/dedicated 5) alert support for customer impact. Want someone to run cordon/drain now.

kevin: I'll cordon nodes gke-infer-usw-1 and gke-infer-usw-3 to stop new pods landing. Doing `kubectl cordon gke-infer-usw-1-abcde` -> node cordoned. `kubectl drain gke-infer-usw-1-abcde --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> drains start.

carla: draining gke-infer-usw-3 now. Noting some stateful inference pods with local checkpoints — using `--delete-local-data` will drop them; switching those to fallback model variant in routing temporarily.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary routing rule updated: inference-route-usw -> prefer eu-west fallback (percentage 30%) to reduce pressure.

maria: good. Sam, start a scale-up on dedicated pool (ded-infer-1) by +4 nodes and a hot-standby on hosted capacity.

sam: scaling ded-infer-1 -> `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize` triggered, instances provisioning. ETA ~7m.

kevin: while draining, noticed kubelet restart logs include `kubelet: runtime service connection lost: rpc error: code = Unavailable`. Containerd shows GPU driver failures.

carla: ran `kubectl describe pod <inference-pod>` for representative crash:```
State:          Running
Last State:     Terminated
  Reason:       OOMKilled
  Exit Code:    137
  Message:      process killed due to memory limit
Events:
  Warning  BackOff  CrashLoopBackOff  3m (x5 over 10m)
```

maria: Customer impact check: telemetry shows increased 5xx and latency for hosted inference in us-west and usw region, ~3-5% of requests returned 502/504 in the last 12m. Not wide, but dipping SLAs for a few key customers. Ping @support-bot to prepare messages.

support-bot: Noted. Drafting status update for affected customers — will include mitigation steps and ETA.

dylan: any quick fix to stop GPU lockups? Driver restart usually helps but requires node restart. We can cordon/replace rather than attempt in-place driver reinstall.

kevin: agree. For safety let's label affected nodes `infra/replaced=true` once cordoned and drain completed, then trigger automated node-recreate via instance-group rolling action.

sam: recreates started for nodes 1 and 3. Node 4 is still NotReady but not yet cordoned. I'll cordon 4 next.

carla: routing team — please confirm fallback model variant has been promoted for pods that lost local data. We need to ensure customers don't see broken responses.

routing: (via infra-bot) fallback promotion confirmed for model v2-small -> v2-small-no-checkpoint. Traffic portion bumped to 30% eu-west.

maria: logging a live incident ticket and linking to this thread. Incident severity set to Sev2 due to customer latency + degraded capacity.

kevin: starting longer-term diagnostics: collecting `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, `dmesg`, kubelet journal, and containerd logs. Pushing them to S3 under `s3://redwood-diagnostics/3723456789/`

sam: container logs show `cudaSetDevice failed: unspecified launch failure` frequently before OOM. Could be multi-process contention + kernel bug.

carla: for immediate safety, we've increased pod eviction threshold to be more aggressive on those nodes (temporary), to avoid some cascading OOMs. Reverting after incident.

maria: support-bot, what's the customer comms text?

support-bot: Draft: "We're investigating a regional GPU node issue affecting inference in US-W. Some requests may see elevated errors or latency. We've routed traffic to fallback capacity and are replacing unhealthy nodes. ETA for recovery 30-45 minutes. We'll update in 15 minutes." Want approval to post.

maria: approve. Post to status. Also open a Slack thread to #support with a short blurb and list of affected customers.

sam: nodes 1 and 3 have been terminated and new instances are provisioning. New nodes show `Ready` as they come up; kubelet versions match and no GPU dmesg on the fresh ones yet.

kevin: node 4 cordoned and drained. Recreate for node 4 queued.

carla: monitoring shows 5xx rate dropping back to baseline after traffic steering and scale up — currently 1.1% over baseline. Not fully resolved; keep watching.

maria: handoff plan: I'm going to stay on until pods stabilize and 5xx back to baseline for 30m. If anyone else needs to take primary, call it out.

kevin: I'll follow up on diagnostics uploads and open a driver bug with vendor if kernel/GPU resets persist.

dylan: docs note: add temporary runbook entry for `gpu-driver-restart-vs-node-recreate` decision matrix. Might speed next time.

maria: final check: are there any customer-facing errors still ongoing? support-bot: any escalations?

support-bot: One enterprise customer (acme-inc) reported degraded throughput; support has escalated and included incident notes. We'll send an ops contact phone update if SLA breach risk > 5% for >60m.

maria: thanks team. I'll update incident ticket and post status update in 15. Staying on watch.

infra-bot: Incident note appended: nodes cordoned and recreated; traffic steered; scale-up performed; customer comms posted.

kevin: closing loop — saved kubelet/journal and containerd logs to S3. Links: `https://s3-redwood/diagnostics/3723456789/*`

maria: last check in this thread at 3723460289: errors down, new nodes healthy. Keeping incident open for postmortem.

carla: adding tag for postmortem: gpu-driver-reset, kubelet-restart, node-recreate, routing-fallback.

maria: thanks all — handoff complete when I've posted the incident summary. :white_check_mark:
